text: The strategy requires a low-stakes deployment context so that online training can minimise the effect of distribution shifts; following Christiano (2021), low-stakes means a few decisions can only cause a small amount of damage, formally that rho times k is small relative to the total value at stake, where rho bounds the utility difference from any single decision and k is the latency before retraining. The authors state that with a perfect training objective total utility could then be kept within a regret bound in rho, k and the number of timesteps T of an aligned system.
title: Low-stakes deployment assumption enabling online training against distribution shift
